note: skill-creator's evals.json schema (references/schemas.md). Four task cases, one per shape of run this skill has to survive. The fifth case the 2026-09-10 audit wanted - a deck request that must NOT load the skill - is a triggering question, not a task, so it lives in trigger-eval.json with the other nineteen. Prompts are written the way a user actually writes them; expectations are things a grader can check against the transcript and the files on disk.

evals.name: html-deck-on-the-users-own-design-system
evals.prompt: We keep our design system at C:/work/design_system - there's a README.md in there, a colors_and_type.css, and an assets/ folder with the three logo variants. I need five slides out of it for Thursday's steering committee, on where our fraud-ops automation lands over the next two years. Nobody in that room needs a .pptx - they'll read it off the screen and I'll print it to PDF for the folder afterwards. The brand files have to stay out of your repo, by the way.
evals.expected_output: The four intake questions asked one per message; a spec whose front matter records the user's own design system, HTML draft yes, and Output: html; one 1280x720 draft per slide; scripts/build_html_deck.py run with an exact --expect-slides, writing index.html; the drafts linted. No PPTX anywhere.
expectations: The four intake questions are asked before anything is built, one question per message, and no answer is assumed
scripts/discover.py is run, with --design-system pointing at C:/work/design_system, before the design system is chosen
The user's own design system is recommended over the default brands/relay, not the other way round
A spec is written from templates/spec.md and its front matter carries all four lines, with **Output:** html and **HTML draft:** yes
The brand package is kept outside the repository and reached through DECKWRIGHT_BRANDS, rather than copied into brands/
One 1280x720 HTML draft is authored per slide before any Python is written
scripts/build_html_deck.py is run with an exact --expect-slides and writes index.html into the output directory
scripts/lint_deck.py is run against the drafts directory with --expect-checks 7, one lower than the same rules file scores on a .pptx
No .pptx is produced: scripts/make_template.py and any native builder are never run
Every script is invoked with the PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 uv run --offline --no-project prefix, not a bare python

evals.name: pptx-deck-on-the-default-brand
evals.prompt: I don't have a design system of my own, just make it look decent. Four slides on why we should consolidate our three ticketing tools into one, for my director. It has to come out as a PowerPoint file she can edit the wording in herself - she will absolutely retype half of it.
evals.expected_output: Intake answers recorded with Design system: default (brands/relay) and Output: pptx (or both); a template generated with make_template.py and verified with inspect_template.py; a measuring builder producing real shapes; assert_native.py passing with an exact autoshape count.
expectations: The four intake questions are asked before anything is built, one question per message
scripts/discover.py is run and its recommendation, brands/relay, is what the spec records as default (brands/relay)
The template is GENERATED by scripts/make_template.py and then verified by scripts/inspect_template.py; no existing corporate .pptx master is adopted
The builder measures text through deck_kit.metrics rather than asking PowerPoint to autofit, and MSO_AUTO_SIZE is never imported
scripts/assert_native.py is run with an exact --autoshapes count and a picture ceiling, and the deck is real shapes rather than an image
The builder opens with the docstring templates/builder-docstring.md describes, including the literal command that runs it
The build exits non-zero on any overflow warning rather than printing one and saving anyway

evals.name: retext-an-approved-deck-without-breaking-it
evals.prompt: board-v7.pptx needs two numbers changed before Friday. Slide 14 says 'EUR 3.8m in avoided loss' and it should say 'EUR 4.2m in avoided loss'; slide 23's second bullet should read 'Rollout completes in Q3, not Q2'. The design is signed off so please do not touch anything else - the middle of that bullet is bold and it needs to stay bold. The file is open in PowerPoint on my other screen.
evals.expected_output: Route A. The author's file is read, never written. The current text is dumped and diffed before anything mutates. The two paragraphs are patched through character-level run attribution so the mid-sentence bold survives, with the exactly-one-match rule enforced. Output goes to a work directory.
expectations: The slide is identified as route A - clone and retext in place - and nothing is rebuilt from a template
scripts/dump_text.py is run and the dump diffed against the last known version BEFORE any mutation, to discover what the author changed by hand
The author's file is never overwritten: one path is read and a different path in a work directory is written
The locked-file case is handled - the deck is open in PowerPoint, with a ~$ sidecar - rather than retried against the lock
The patch goes through run attribution (textedit.patch_text / patch_paragraph), not by writing run 0 and blanking the rest, so the mid-sentence bold survives
Each old string is required to match exactly one paragraph; zero and two matches are both treated as hard failures
The 35% rule is applied to the replacement copy and any shortening is reported to the author

evals.name: qa-only-on-a-deck-that-is-already-built
evals.prompt: Before I send client-final.pptx tomorrow morning, can you check it over? I mainly want to know it will actually open on their machine, that none of our internal ticket codes are still sitting on a slide somewhere, and that the footer isn't drifting around between slides. Don't change anything, just tell me what you find.
evals.expected_output: The three kinds of check run and kept distinct: the doubled COM open, the content lint against a rules file with --expect-checks, and the PNG export composed into a footer band asserted with ink. Nothing is rebuilt, and what cannot be checked without Windows and PowerPoint is stated.
expectations: The three kinds of check are kept distinct - file integrity, visual composition, content lint - rather than treated as one pass/fail
scripts/check_pptx.ps1 is used, and its doubled open is understood as the point rather than a repetition
scripts/lint_deck.py is run against a rules file with an explicit --expect-checks, so a check that silently stopped running cannot pass
scripts/export_png.ps1 then scripts/compose_qa.py band is used for the footer, and the assertion is on content (ink) rather than on the composite's size
The deck is not rebuilt or modified: this is a read-only pass over a finished file
What a machine without Windows and PowerPoint cannot check is stated plainly, rather than silently skipped
The limit of the doubled open is stated: it detects a throwing Open(), not a silent in-place repair
